wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.ephemeral_event: Transient sync/federation/app signal; MUST NOT be persisted as durable Event Envelope history.

admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a self-authored proof bound to the subject principal's identity (DID-bound signature / proof of possession with bounded freshness). Reducer MUST verify actor == subject and a fresh, replay-protected proof; no capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing or stale proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-DID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by one or more named capability actions listed in admission_capabilities. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant per capability-action-registry. Fail-closed.

registry_rules: Standard ck.* effect kinds MUST appear in this registry when used by a DataEvent effect, Control Move effect, or Event Envelope payload router.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.
Entries with wire_scope=ephemeral_event MUST be carried only on ephemeral channels and MUST NOT advance Seal coverage, governance state_root, or reducer state.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

Reducer-input durable kinds MAY declare cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, and (cas_register only) initial_value. cell_family is a stable ck.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, a payload field path, or a composite descriptor; bottom is reject or expose. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any DataEvent or Control Move effect has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` Control Move predicates implements singleton-once-set cells.

Registered exemption: protocol-singleton cells that are not written through a single event_kind are NOT indexed here. Currently the only such cell family is ck.component.notary.v1 (per-Realm notary cell, lattice=cas_register, bottom=reject): its genesis value comes from the ck.realm.create payload notary object and subsequent changes are ordinary notary-finalized Control Moves; its canonical definition lives in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 4.4. Any future cell family without a single writer kind MUST be added to this exemption list explicitly.

Lattice MUST be one of: core types or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log; or extension types lww_register, rga (only declarable on cells with cell_role in {ui_affordance, content, draft, cosmetic} and only valid for receivers that implement ck.profile.collaborative_text.v1; receivers without that profile MUST fail closed with unsupported_lattice_type when an event_kind references a cell using lww_register or rga). Authorization, policy, notary, membership, and lifecycle cells MUST NOT use lww_register or rga.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent effects are locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move effects are finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST list the authorizing action(s) in admission_capabilities. Enforced by lint_artifacts.py; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ck.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.

event_kinds.payload: Realm official or sponsoring organization statement

Typed Realm link graph edge. link_kind declares governance / discoverability / import-export / confidential-extension semantics; it is never generic parent/child containment and never implicitly propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Realm preview / peek policy for directory card, stripped state, history stub, and plaintext history snippet projections

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. payload = {realm_id, strand_id}; reducer projects payload.strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify the referenced strand_id already exists in this Realm (a projected, non-tombstoned Strand); a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. Strand-side is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage; clients discover the default Strand deterministically from the Realm projection default_strand_id or the Strand projection is_default, NOT from any UUID-reuse implementation detail. Authorization is the standard Realm-admin gate (hold ck.realm.admin, or the same-name action ck.realm.set_default_strand).
Enabled Realm policy components set. Payload MUST carry monotonic policy_revision; reducer rejects rollback or gaps and policy_frontier_digest MUST cover policy_revision.

Constraints on member delivery_binding: which binding_source values are admissible, which recipient services are allowed, which endorsers are required, whether DID Document fallback / unroutable membership are permitted, who may sign rebind. Governs reducer acceptance of ck.member.state{membership=join}.delivery_binding (see governance/join-policy.md §5.1).

Realm read receipt disclosure policy (disclosure / visibility / scope_overrides_allowed / allow_child_privacy_tightening_against_required); see zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5 for the compliance-floor escape switch
Realm moderation policy (blocklists, allowlists, content filters)
Plaintext-visible services declaration outside E2EE boundary
Per-parent inheritance policy; one entry per source Realm
Realm tombstone lifecycle facet (terminal pointer to successor)
Realm destroy lifecycle facet (terminal decommission marker)
Circle create (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary). Initializes independent MLS group and epoch-0 governance binding only when encryption_profile=mls_rfc9420. See zh/models/circle.md §3, §5.
Circle patch (ck.patch.v1 with path NOT containing realm_id / encryption_profile). Modifies title / summary / display / directory_visibility / join_rule / history_visibility.
Circle tombstone (terminal). Triggers lifecycle cascade per zh/models/circle.md §9.2.

Circle membership state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ck.member.state (invite/join/knock/leave/ban), scoped to a Circle. Reducer MUST first validate the target actor is a parent Realm `join` member, otherwise failed_precondition reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

Reducer-derived: Circle sub-seal commits opaque sub_seal_head_digest to the Realm Seal stream at the Circle's profile-defined cadence. MUST use time-based ticks + empty-batch commitment to avoid leaking activity frequency. See zh/models/circle.md §10.2.

Issuer-signed endorsement that a subject DID (typically an agent / service / hosted actor) is accountable_principal_ids the issuer for a declared scope (employment / contracted_service / agent_operator / etc.). Required to verify `Actor Profile.accountable_principal_ids[]` entries; reducer strips unverified DIDs from accountable_principal_ids. See zh/models/actor.md §3.3.1.

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ck.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ck.profile.update patch semantics.

Strand business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at; ck.strand.update patch on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on the Strand's discussion track that 'references' this event, and the event log's own actor_id / created_at is the audit source. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=strand_already_terminal; state=archived yields strand_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond these hard invariants.

Unified Strand tracks patch. payload.patch uses ck.patch.v1 against the Strand.tracks map: keys are track names (e.g. `synthesis`, `discussion`), values are patch ops that may toggle enabled, set is_primary, or modify profile / metadata on a track entry. Atomic across multiple tracks.

Strand move between Spaces (target_space_id in payload). Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (board_space_id, strand_id); the contains Relation list_space_id->strand_id is derived from cell value, not a separate truth source. Plane ruling (CBA): ck.component.strand.position.v1 defaults to sealed=true (control plane), so ck.strand.move is a Control Move carrying seal_basis; Realm schema MAY redeclare the cell family as data-plane mv_register + user-pick or per-object sequencer per authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.4 and models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6.

Strand reorder within Space. Writes the same cell as ck.strand.move; effect.list_space_id MUST equal head_eq.list_space_id (rank-only update). Plane ruling follows ck.strand.move: same cell family, same default sealed=true control-plane declaration (models/realm-and-space.md section 3.6).

Set or clear a per-(strand, actor) watch subscription. Writes a cas_register cell keyed by (strand_id, watcher_actor_id). Payload carries level in {mentions_only, participating, all, muted} (or null to clear, equivalent to mentions_only). Default invariant: payload.watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope actor_id, unless writer holds ck.strand.watch.set.others. Cross-actor writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ck.audit.accessed event with access_kind=watch_set_others. The watches Relation (actor --watches--> strand) is a derived projection of this cell, not a separate truth source — direct ck.relation.create relation_kind=watches MUST schema_violation. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.
Space create (board / list / swimlane / calendar bucket / etc.)
Space metadata update (title, rank, kind-specific fields)

Space parent declaration. Parent is another ck:space: or null; cross-Realm parent is navigation only and never propagates Realm membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.
Space archive (UI-level grouping archive; contained Strands MUST be relocated or follow archive)
Space restore (transition state archived -> active; only valid when current state == archived; tombstoned Spaces MUST NOT be restored)
Space tombstone (irreversible; contained Strands MUST be relocated before)
Message-scoped redaction; does not grant generic redaction authority
Generic redaction envelope for non-message objects/events and profile-declared content trimming

Morph schema_refs[] migration. First-class event for evolving a Morph's schema_refs[] without bypassing audit / capability gates. Carries (from_schema_refs[], to_schema_refs[], compatibility_class, migration_evidence?). Required capability ck.morph.schema_migrate (high risk tier; see capability-action-registry.json). compatibility_class = additive | breaking | transformation; core reducers MUST reject breaking/transformation unless the Realm declares ck.profile.morph.schema_migration_transformations.v1. See zh/models/morph.md §4.1 S3.

Morph business-progression stage transition. Single source of truth for mutating Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at; ck.morph.update / ck.morph.schema_migrate patches on those paths MUST be rejected (forbidden-wire). The payload intentionally carries no reason / note / explanation field — rationale belongs in a Message on an associated discussion track that 'references' this event. Reducer enforces hard invariants from zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3: state=redacted yields failed_precondition reason=morph_already_terminal; state=archived yields morph_not_active; same-value self-transition is accepted but does NOT update stage_changed_at; reducer overwrites any wire-supplied stage_changed_at with the event's created_at.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_principal_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, expires_at, and approval_evidence.

Agent signing key revocation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_revoke_payload and bind agent_principal_id, key_id, revoked_at, and revoked_by; the revocation's control-plane basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and its cutoff is the accepted Seal covering the Move.

Agent signing key rotation. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_rotate_payload; key_id names the retiring key and replacement_key_id names the new key under the same accountable_principal_id with equivalent or narrower agent_key_scope.

Agent lifecycle transition to paused state (CKP-0008 §4.11). Auth Server MUST reject new agent session grants for this principal; existing tokens fail closed within the revocation freshness window. Reversible via ck.agent.resume.

Agent lifecycle transition from paused to active (CKP-0008 §4.11). Reducer MUST re-validate controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability_grant freshness; any failure rejects the resume.

Agent lifecycle terminal state (CKP-0008 §4.11). MUST fan-out ck.agent.key.revoke for all active agent keys, ck.capability.revoke for all active grants, and runtime endpoint revocation. Terminal — no transition out.

Agent-initiated draft proposal (CKP-0008 §4.8). Submitted by agent runtime; Principal Server materializes accepted drafts into controller-owned ck.agent.draft.v1 account-data after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. MUST NOT enter shared Realm history.
Agent-initiated action request (CKP-0008 §4.8). Carries proposed_action, target descriptor, and content digest. Awaits controller approval before generating shared event.

Controller approval of a draft / action request (CKP-0008 §4.8.1). Binds draft_id, content digest, target descriptor, proposed_action, approved payload digest, approval expiry, and single-use nonce. Publish executor MUST atomic-consume the nonce; reuse fails closed (reason=approval_already_consumed).
Controller rejection of a draft / action request (CKP-0008 §4.8.1). Draft transitions to rejected; agent runtime MUST NOT continue publish attempts.
Holder-private consent declaration: 'I consent to receive <consent_scope> from <peer>'
Revoke a previously granted consent (shares the ck.consent.grant cell; semantically a remove on the consent or_set)
Principal-scoped contact request fact. Issuer is requester; target holder must respond with accepted/rejected.
Principal-scoped contact acceptance fact. Issuer is original request target and MUST reference target-controlled consent grants.
Principal-scoped contact rejection fact. Issuer is original request target and does not write consent.
Principal-scoped contact tombstone fact. Issuer ends their own side of a contact and may revoke contact-managed consent dots.
Principal-scoped binding from unordered participant pair to canonical DM Realm and main Strand.
Realm-scoped profile override. payload.target_realm_id is the target Realm and no Space boundary is created.
Key backup active series selection for one principal and backup_class.

Push route binding for a (recipient_service_did, principal, device, push_route) tuple. Carries push_target_id, push_gateway_did, encryption_key, capabilities. Stored as actor-private state on the recipient Principal Server only; MUST NOT be replicated to Principal Servers outside the binding's recipient_service_did context.
MLS commit or Welcome processing failure diagnostic

Auditable access marker for privileged reads or privacy-sensitive paired writes. E2EE compliance release uses ck.audit.release; ck.audit.accessed remains for non-release audit pairs such as Circle metadata audit, watch_set_others, late recovery, and policy reads.

Audit Applet Binding. Declares that an audit applet/service may request staged historical release sessions for a specific Realm or Circle effective_scope. Binding is control-plane only: it does not add the applet to MLS, does not subscribe it to realtime sync, and does not grant plaintext/history keys. Bindings are non-retroactive: activation_frontier_digest / first_auditable_epoch define the earliest eligible material, and later policy changes MUST NOT expand eligibility for already encrypted messages.
Audit release session request. Must reference an active ck.audit.applet_binding and a bounded historical target range or target_refs.
Audit release session authorization by a scoped approver. Approves only the intersection of request, binding, policy, and effective_scope.
Member-visible notice for an audit release session. Circle-scoped notices are visible only to the target Circle audience and authorized moderators/admins.

Sealed audit release manifest. Records exactly which historical target_refs or sealed epochs were released, to whom, under which binding/session/notice/policy. Current active epoch release is forbidden; sealed epoch releases must reference sealed_by_commit_ref.
Close an audit release session and freeze its final release_refs.
Signed hard-erasure receipt. Attests deletion outcome and retained verification stub within an issuer-declared storage boundary; does not prove independent third-party copies disappeared.

Range-bound completeness attestation. Distinct from ck.audit.ryw_receipt (per-event read-your-writes hint) and ck.event_batch_receipt (set-bound integrity hint): this attestation asserts completeness over an explicit (from_frontier, to_frontier) + per-actor seq interval range. Issuer commits to having observed every reducer-input event in scope; witness quorum or independent seal backing is required for non-self-attested deployments. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §4.2.
Lift a previously sealed moderation decision (observed-remove/supersede the referenced decision in ck.component.moderation_state.v1)

Submit an appeal against an existing ck.moderation.decision. Writes the appeal cell to state=submitted. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal strand).
Reviewer acknowledges the appeal and transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Identifies the reviewing actor and target appeal. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Reviewer's verdict on the appeal: uphold (decision stands) / overturn (decision reversed, emits ck.moderation.decision.lift) / modify (decision adjusted). Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Closes the appeal from submitted / under_review / decided via reviewer close, appellant withdrawal, or a deployment's authorized close service. close is a manual/authorized action; the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer or cool-off duration (deployment/Realm policy decides). Schema: ck.schema.moderation_appeal.v1.

Read cursor advance event (actor-private). Writes the actor's latest read position for a given (realm_id, read_scope) tuple. Was historically named ck.read.cursor; renamed to align the event_kind, capability action, schema id and typed ID prefix on a single noun root read_cursor.

Invite create. Directed v1 invite payloads carry invitee plus invite_delivery_target and introduction_evidence_digest; raw locator tokens and invite_receive_policy state are private and MUST NOT enter the durable Realm event.

reducer_effects: match pending ck.invite.third_party by invite_id and token_commitment
re-check verification_service_did against current effective Realm allowlist
deduplicate (invite_id, claim_nonce) and token_commitment before accepting
transition invite cell pending -> claimed and materialize subject-bound membership proposal
expire and clean pending invite material before claim acceptance when expires_at <= now

Canonical plaintext keybag opened from a ck.schema.key_backup.v1 envelope.
Proof binding a key-backup read/decrypt action to one recovery session, requesting device, backup object, selected series, ciphertext digest, and accepted proof transcript.

Bound to the Principal Control Realm via signed publish / rotate / share-revoke; receivers MUST reject recovery / rotate / ck.device.authorize and cross-signing-reset evidence whose proof family is not allowed by the currently accepted recovery policy. Closed request/response DTO bundle for ck.self.keys.upload.create, query, claim, and key backup put/list/delete responses.

Canonical ServiceDescribe response for ck.server.query.describe and per-surface describe operations: base service metadata plus claim-level partitions (supported_operations / implemented_features / claimed_profiles / verified_profiles / experimental_features / compat_surfaces). Enforces development_mode=true => verified_profiles=[]. compat_surfaces is limited to external interop surfaces. See service-surface.md §3.0.

Defs-only shared typed-ID patterns (e.g. circle_id) referenced cross-file by morph and relation schemas so a single id-form change propagates without inline drift. Not an object/event schema. See zh/models/common-fields.md §6.

Canonical response body for the delivery_binding_stale federation signal (member delivery-binding rebind handover): new_recipient_service_did, handover_frontier, and the verifiable handover_proof. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.1 and error-code-registry.json (delivery_binding_stale / delivery_binding_handover_proof_invalid).

Canonical wire schema for client query / projection (query_request) and search (search_request) request bodies plus reusable filter / sort / relation-query $defs. The OpenAPI QueryRequestBody / SearchRequestBody / QueryFilter / FieldFilter / BooleanFilter / SortSpec / RelationQuery components $ref this file so there is a single source of truth. Human-readable semantics: zh/conformance/query-schema.md.
Canonical DTO bundle for service operation request/response shapes migrated out of OpenAPI inline components.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form ck:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ck:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference; distinct from ck:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Realm-scoped pseudonymous credential reference; validated by the E2EE profile. v1 core uses Realm as the boundary; Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Seal hash.
Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
Store the scope string as an opaque deployment-level identifier; it appears in server describe, Realm policy, and high-risk proof transcripts.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk proofs (e.g. ck.cross_signing.reset §14.1). NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kinds.description: Moderation appeal ID — opaque key for the ck.component.moderation.appeal.v1 cell. Created by ck.moderation.appeal.submit; referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.

Agent interop session ID. Note the cross-surface naming: this typed ID uses the short form `agent_interop_session`, while the corresponding event kinds use the full form `ck.agent.interop_session.{start,status,result}` and capability actions use `ck.agent.interop_session.{start,cancel,stream_status,attach_artifact,read_transcript}`. The three surfaces all refer to the same session concept; downstream tooling MUST NOT assume `ck:<event-prefix>:<uuid>` mechanical derivation.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Audit Applet Binding ID. Created by ck.audit.applet_binding and referenced by audit session request/authorize/notice/release events.
Audit release session ID. Threads ck.audit.session.request, authorize, notice, release, and close events for one bounded historical audit window.
Audit release manifest ID. Created by ck.audit.release for a sealed historical release under an active audit binding/session.

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_class). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by ck.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery strands to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form

SFU-local participant handle (CKP-0010). Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_service_did, issued_at_bucket)` by the media service token issuer. MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in `ck.call.state.participants[].participant_identity` and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `ck:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use ck:grant:<uuid>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.

Device identifier (ck:device:<uuid>). A device is a typed ID scoped to an owning principal, NOT a DID and NOT an actor principal. Device keys are registered as verification methods under the owning principal DID via ck.device.authorize.
Signed capability grant object ID used by ck.schema.capability.v1 and grant/revoke references.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery strand. Referenced by ck.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Cokret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of query, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex query body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Cokret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Cokret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Cokret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

operations.notes: Managed-DID (account-authority) device enrollment, device-lifecycle.md §5.4 / key-management.md §5.0.6. The authenticated session asks its designated enrollment authority to mint a service_attested ck.device.authorize for this session's own device; the authority signs with its persistent enrollment key (never the principal SSK) and returns the full Event. The caller submits it verbatim to POST /_cokret/self/events. Distinct from pair_device (§2.1), which lands an existing-device SAS/QR approval and carries a pairing_code; enroll_device is the bootstrap / first-device path where no sibling device can approve.

Account Authority single-call grant exchange. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome; any Principal-side local session provisioning is internal to the Account Authority. There is no separate client-visible grant-to-bearer exchange step: the client presents the returned ck.session.grant directly to /_cokret/self/* with a DPoP proof (api-conventions §3.3). For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges the authorization code at the issuer token_endpoint and validates issuer/state/nonce/redirect_uri/principal/device/audience binding before issuing the grant; the client MAY omit principal_id at first sign-in, in which case the Account Authority derives/mints the principal DID and returns it in SessionGrantOutcome.principal_id.

DPoP-bound session-grant rotation (account-lifecycle §4.1, device-lifecycle §3.3). An authorized device presents a DPoP holder proof for the grant's cnf.jkt and rotates onto a fresh grant; the old grant is single-use revoked. Account Authority-local op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority lower-level grant-only logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): DPoP holder proof revokes the grant and finishes the underlying browser session, terminating the rotation chain. Ordinary client hard logout should use ck.gate.account.command.logout so Account Authority can also terminate Principal-side local account session state. HTTP-only lower-level op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and a holder-proof challenge) and learns whether it is active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_cokret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): terminate the grant rotation chain/browser session and the Principal-side local account session + device session record, then drop the device's queued to-device. Distinct from revoke_session (session-token-only). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Optional Account Authority browser redirect landing / handoff for deployments that use an OIDC redirect URI under /_cokret/gate/account. It MUST NOT issue or return SessionGrantOutcome, ck.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance remains ck.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.

source_signature_anchor.node_to_applet: Source-Service-DID current service DID verification method; Destination-Service-DID MUST equal the Applet registration service_did.
source_signature_anchor.applet_to_cokret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; DID part MUST equal Source-Service-DID and the active effective install service_did.

operations.notes: Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. HTTP binding is POST because the request is a batch command against a queue collection, deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key), and does not replace a single URI-addressed message resource. Queue pruning is only via ck.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages from=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.
Writes requester-side ck.contact.requested fact and requester-side consent grants for requested scopes; MUST NOT write target consent or accepted fact.
Target-side accept/reject of a contact request. Accept writes target-controlled consent grants; reject writes no consent.
Holder contact projection from contact facts plus consent-derived directional scopes; account-data contact notes are local decoration only.
Holder-side contact tombstone. Default revocation is limited to contact-managed active consent dots.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ck.self.contact.command.tombstone(block_peer) blocked_subjects writes.
Idempotent resolver for accepted contacts. Requires accepted contact projection and direct_message consent; create=true creates canonical DM Realm, main Strand, and binding.

Builds a ck.circle.create Operation in the named parent Realm and routes it through the local accept pipeline. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Builds ck.circle.member.state. Activating another actor requires ck.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule.
Builds ck.circle.member.state with membership=leave for the path actor_id.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.
Builds ck.circle.archive; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active).
Builds ck.circle.tombstone (terminal). Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter / include_completeness parameter set, same response shape including optional range_completeness). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. Non-HTTP transports MUST use the canonical ck.self.events.query.scan binding (SelfEvents/Query / self.events.query.scan), not expose this variant as a separate gRPC or MQ operation.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ck.self.events.query.scan for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Durable self event submission, including ck.invite.claim. For ck.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer is the authoritative state machine: it MUST match token_commitment, re-check verification_service_did allowlist against current Realm policy, reject claim_nonce replay, perform pending -> claimed / membership-proposal effects, and run expiry cleanup before accepting.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ck.self.events.query.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ck.peer.events.query.scan. Semantically identical to GET /_cokret/peer/events; use it when federation selectors or filters are too large or sensitive for query strings.

Federation peer event reference resolution for missing prev_refs / causal references. Requires authorized federation peer service authentication and applies the same reference-disclosure and history-visibility rules as peer event query.

Federation peer event push. Body is EventsSubmitFederationRequestBody and the caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ck.invite.claim events are still decided by the destination Realm reducer, which MUST enforce token_commitment, current allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, membership proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup; peer ingress prechecks are not state authority.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_did, a ck.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server contact fact delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-DID equal to contact_address.recipient_service_did, and a signed ck.contact.* envelope the recipient projects into the target holder's contact projection without re-signing.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for ck.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries ck.presence, ck.typing, ck.receipt.read, and ck.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Media service token exchange operation (CKP-0010). Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ck.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / cokret-native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Read the currently accepted ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Publish a signed ck.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation for the authenticated principal. HTTP binding is POST because the principal/authority is derived from authenticated proof and signed policy state rather than a URI-addressed resource slot. Servers MUST verify auth_data.signed_fields, signature authority, version monotonicity, and supersedes linkage before accepting.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_cokret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ck.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Builds a ck.realm.link Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id. The reducer runs realm_link_* validators (cycle detection, self-reference, kind validation); a rejected payload returns 422 with the canonical reason code (e.g. realm_link_cycle, realm_link_self_reference).

Writes a tombstoning ck.realm.link Move (status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple. link_kind defaults to governed_by; callers may override via the link_kind query param.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ck.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).
Reads the projected ck.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_org_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Builds a ck.realm.policy_server Move (admission capability ck.policy.manage). Reducer validates URL scheme and on_timeout enum. This admin DTO is a simplified projection of the canonical payload (server_id/endpoint/public_keys/applies_to/fail_mode).
Tombstones the per-Realm ck.realm.policy_server cell so callers fall back to the governed_by chain or local-only capability check. Empty success response.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ck.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Writes a Realm moderation-policy override (ck.realm.moderation_policy). Only the Realm owner may write; an override that loosens an action an organization policy denies requires explicit organization approval embedded in the document, otherwise the server returns requires_organization_approval.
Lists holder-private consent cells where the caller is holder or peer. Each cell projects the current effective consent for a (holder, peer, consent_scope).
Reads one consent cell. Requires peer and consent_scope query params; caller MUST be holder or that peer. Returns not_found when no cell exists.
Builds a ck.consent.grant Control Move on the holder's consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Builds a ck.consent.revoke Control Move enumerating the active grant dots for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope). Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.
Opens a pending consent request from the authenticated peer to a holder. peer_did defaults to and MUST equal the authenticated actor; the holder account MUST exist.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.
Reads one account_data entry by data_type key. Returns not_found when the key is unset.

Builds a ck.account_data.set actor-private write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.
Deletes one account_data entry and fans out an actor-private update to the holder's other devices.

Builds a ck.read_cursor.advance actor-private write for (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position). Multi-device convergence is by HLC max with device_id tiebreak; the cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface for reducer-maintained Space lifecycle projection rows scoped by realm_id. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface for a single document Morph projection. It returns authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model data for the addressed Morph; canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Holder-bound service wrapper around ck.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; profile_fields.bio is the canonical personal bio field and avatar_url is not accepted on the Cokret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with ck.self.events.stream.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (self.events.stream.subscribe = per-Realm event log; self.account.stream.subscribe = account-aggregate). `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same principal/device/filter scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After. Presence changes are sent through ck.self.ephemeral.command.send, not this read-only stream subscription.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ck.self.device_messages.command.ack.

success_shape_kind_definitions.service_describe: ServiceDescribe object returned by a describe endpoint.
success_shape_kind_definitions.schema_resource: Response body is a canonical artifact JSON Schema resource.
success_shape_kind_definitions.inline_response: Endpoint-specific inline object schema in OpenAPI.
success_shape_kind_definitions.operation_result: Generic OperationResult envelope; operation row MUST carry generic_binding.
success_shape_kind_definitions.event_stream: Long-lived event stream rather than a single JSON success body.
success_shape_kind_definitions.metadata_headers: Metadata-only success expressed through HTTP headers.

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ck.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ck.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

actions.notes: Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ck.audit.accessed pair (same model as ck.strand.watch.set.others).

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ck.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ck.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ck.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.

event_mapping_kind_definitions.same_name: Action maps one-to-one to an identically named durable event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.non_event_surface: Action authorizes read/projection/signaling behavior that does not emit a durable reducer event.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.aggregate_admin: Action intentionally covers a bounded administrative family of event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.polymorphic_object: Action covers the same object-lifecycle verb across multiple object event kinds.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.scope_suffix_variant: Action adds actor/scope/role qualifiers while reducer admission targets a shared event kind.
event_mapping_kind_definitions.operation_verb: Action token names an operation/command verb that does not match its target event kind name(s); reducer admission resolves the resulting event kind(s) via target_event_kinds. Literal action matching per the actions[] rule applies; carries no aggregate-admin family semantics.
